subject: Post-call recap: deployment options & SOC2/BAA evidence request
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Kent <alice.kent@govcare.org>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call recap: deployment options & SOC2/BAA evidence request

Hi Alice —

Great to meet you and the GovCare team earlier. Quick recap of what we discussed and the evidence/next steps we’d need to qualify deployment mode options for your PHI workload. I’ve summarized tradeoffs up front and then listed the doc requests below.

Recommendation summary (based on our call):
- If GovCare will store/transmit PHI and needs full audit and network isolation: Private (VPC/on-prem) is the conservative choice.
- If you need predictable throughput with an SLA but want Redwood to manage infra: Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) + BAA is the middle ground.
- If data can be pseudonymized or only token-level PHI passes through short-lived sessions, Hosted API is possible but will need a review and specific safeguards (prefix/KV caching off for PHI, strict retention config).

Evidence / documents requested to continue qualification:
1) Confirmation whether GovCare will store PHI at rest in our systems or whether data will be processed and returned to your environment only. (answer: store vs pass-through)
2) SOC 2 Type II report (we can provide our latest; see attachment).
3) Completed BAA (we attached our template; please mark changes).
4) Network diagram showing your VPCs, ingress/egress, and where model calls originate.
5) Data flow diagram for the feature(s) that will touch PHI: which services send/receive tokens, retention points.
6) Any customer-specific audit requirements (e.g., quarterly penetration testing, log retention > 1 year).
7) Hosting constraints: must be on-prem? Required regions?

Attachments included from our side: redwood_baa_template_v1.pdf, redwood_soc2_summary_2026.pdf

Proposed next steps:
- Please send the answers + network/data flow by EOD next Tue (2027-07-27) if possible.
- We’ll schedule a 60-minute technical workshop (product + security) once we have your network/data flow to validate: 1) feasible deployment modes and 2) approximate lead times.
- If you want pricing early, Priya (cc’d) will draft a Dedicated vs Private estimate based on throughput/peak token forecasts.

Happy to be flexible on timing — thanks again for the conversation.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0129

From: Alice Kent <alice.kent@govcare.org>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: GovCare Security <security@govcare.org>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 09:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment options & SOC2/BAA evidence request

Thanks Monica — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- GovCare will be processing PHI (patient notes, identifiers). We will not persist PHI on Redwood-managed storage unless we explicitly choose a workflow that stores model outputs; default should be pass-through and short retention.
- We need a BAA in place before any integration work begins.
- SOC2 Type II is required for vendor risk; please confirm the date range for the report you attached and whether you have any SOC2 audit exceptions.
- For Dedicated vs Private: our security team prefers private VPC/air-gapped options for any system that can re-assemble PHI. Is on-prem deployment supported? If so, what is the expected lead time?

I attached our GovCare security profile (govcare_security_profile.xlsx) — it contains our baseline controls and any additional evidence we usually request.

Can you also confirm: latency SLOs for Dedicated vs Private vs Hosted for a 2k token request? And whether key management options (customer-managed KMS/HSM) are available in Private mode?

Thanks — Alice
Alice Kent, Director of Product Compliance | GovCare Health
alice.kent@govcare.org

On Sun, Jul 25, 2027 at 3:12 PM Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Great to meet you and the GovCare team earlier. Quick recap...
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Kent <alice.kent@govcare.org>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 11:23:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment options & SOC2/BAA evidence request

Thanks Alice — good questions. Answers below and a proposed timeline.

Short answers up front:
- SOC2 report: redwood_soc2_summary_2026.pdf covers the period Jan–Dec 2026; no open exceptions. Full SOC2 Type II report can be provided under NDA if required.
- On-prem: yes, we support an on-prem package for customers who must run in their datacenter/air-gapped environment. That path has the most ramp (estimate 8–10 weeks for an initial validation + install).
- Dedicated: supports customer BAA and isolated GPU pools; typical lead time 3–4 weeks once contract and capacity are agreed. Latency SLOs: Dedicated ~35–120ms per token (depending on model), Private/on-prem depends on your infra profile (we’ll validate in workshop), Hosted (shared) has higher variability and we don’t recommend for PHI unless you can ensure pass-through/pseudonymization.
- KMS/HSM: customer-managed KMS is supported in Private and Dedicated; HSM integrations available for on-prem customers.

Requested evidence (we pulled items from your sheet):
- SOC2 Type II (we provided a summary; will send full report under NDA).
- Signed BAA (please review our template — redwood_baa_template_v1.pdf — and mark any redlines).
- Network diagram + IP allowlist requirements.
- Data flow diagram for PHI paths, including whether any outputs are persisted.
- Retention requirements and log retention policy target (you mentioned 2 years on call; confirm).
- Any third-party penetration-test reports we should expect to align to.

Proposed path and timeline (based on current inputs):
Option A — Private VPC / On‑prem (recommended if you require strict control): 8–10 weeks (validation, install, integration), supports KMS/HSM, full audit logging, long retention options.
Option B — Dedicated capacity + BAA (recommended if you want Redwood-managed infra with SLA): 3–4 weeks after legal/contract, isolated GPU pools, customer KMS supported.
Option C — Hosted (fastest): immediate, but only for non-PII/PHI or heavily pseudonymized workflows with strict retention config — not recommended for broad PHI processing.

Next steps I’ll take:
1) Create an internal security JIRA (GOV-1284) and link required evidence; Rishi will be assigned to lead the audit review.
2) Share full SOC2 under NDA if you confirm NDA; share the BAA draft for legal review.
3) Schedule the 60-min technical workshop with your infra/security team — propose Wed 2027-07-28 10:00 AM ET or Thu 2027-07-29 2:00 PM ET. Which works?

Priya — can you prepare a rough pricing delta (Dedicated vs Private) based on a 10k peak tokens/minute profile? I’ll share the network/data flow once Alice returns the diagram.

Alice — thank you for the govcare_security_profile.xlsx — we’ll review and call out any gaps.

Best,
Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
